title: ItemDef
description:
A single item definition from JSON type `"ITEM"`.

CDDA has many subtypes of ITEM (GUN, AMMO, COMESTIBLE, TOOL, etc.) that all share this same struct with different fields populated.

abstract_.description: Abstract flag (not a real game object)

ammo_type.description: Ammo type (string or array of strings for magazines).

armor.description: Armor values — array of body part armor data (CDDA format).

color.description: Color for map display (can be string, map, or array in CDDA data).

conductive.description: Whether item is conductive (electric damage passes through).

container.description: Container (the container item this comes in)

count_mode.description: How charges work for this item.

covers_head.description: Whether item covers the wearer's head (for helmets).

damage.description: Ammo damage — number, structured object `{"damage_type": "bullet", "amount": 25}`, or typed array.  Uses `RawValue` because CDDA ammo damage objects mix string and numeric values (unlike `MeleeDamage`).

dispersion.description: Inherent dispersion (accuracy penalty) of the ammunition.

fun.description: Fun rating (for comestibles / food). For books, see `read_fun` instead.

longest_side.description: Longest dimension of the item (for pocket fitting).

looks_like.description: Item looks like another item for display

martial_art.description: Book: martial art style this book teaches (e.g. "style_aikido").

material.description: Materials this item is made from.

max_level.description: Book: max skill level this book teaches.

melee_damage.description: Damage data for melee (can be object or number).

pocket_data.description: If set, this item is a container with the given pocket data.

range.description: Effective range of the ammunition (in tiles).

read_fun.description: Book: fun from reading (separate from food `fun`).

recoil.description: Recoil contributed by firing this ammunition.

required_level.description: Book: required skill level to read.

revert_to.description: Revert to item ID (for activated tools).

rigid.description: Whether the item is rigid (volume doesn't change when empty).

stackable.description: If true, item is a pseudo item (used internally, not a real object).

time.description: Book: reading time (CDDA time string like "30 m" or "8 m"). Parsed via `Time` which accepts "30 m", "1 h", bare numbers, etc.

tool.description: Tool requirement (tool ID string or map of tool IDs to counts).

tool_ammo.description: Tool ammo (ammunition type(s) this tool accepts).

ArmorMaterialLayer.description: A material layer in an armor piece.

covered_by_mat.description: Percentage of the armor piece covered by this material.

BodyPartArmor.description:
A body part armor data — the individual elements in the `"armor"` array on items.

CDDA items store armor as an array of these objects, each describing how a piece of armor covers a specific body part.

Example: ```json { "encumbrance_modifiers": ["NONE"], "coverage": 100, "covers": ["head"], "specifically_covers": ["head_crown", "head_forehead"] } ```

covers.description: Coverages body parts (single string or array of strings).

encumbrance.description: Encumbrance value (single value or range `[min, max]`).

layers.description: Clothing layers this armor piece occupies (e.g. "NORMAL", "OUTER").

material.description: Materials layered in this armor piece.

max_contains_volume.description: Max volume the pocket/armor can hold.

CddaColor.description:
A color value in CDDA can be a simple name, a list of names (random), or a structured map with foreground/background.

Examples: - `"red"` - `["white", "light_gray"]` - `{"fg": "red", "bg": "blue"}`

anyOf.description: Structured color with foreground (and optional background / season variants).

CddaColorStructured.description: A structured color with optional foreground and background.

CddaDuration.description:
A time duration value from CDDA.

CDDA uses human-readable time strings in many places. Examples: `"1 day"`, `"14 days"`, `"30 minutes"`, `"6 h"`.

Also accepts raw numeric second values.

CddaPrice.description:
Item price.

CDDA prices can be plain integers (in cents) or strings with currency units like `"13 cent"`, `"16 USD"`, `"34 USD"`.

anyOf.description: String with currency unit (e.g. "13 cent", "16 USD").

ComestibleType.description:
Comestible type — the `"comestible_type"` field on COMESTIBLE items.

CDDA uses "INVALID" for items that are not actually comestible but have COMESTIBLE type for other reasons (e.g., chemicals, non-food items).

oneOf.description: "INVALID" — item is not actually a comestible (used for chemicals, etc.)

CountMode.description:
How charges work for this item.

CDDA has long-standing bugs from confusing charges-count meaning; `CountMode` makes this explicit.

anyOf.description: Item is not a stackable/charged item.
Item that stacks by count (e.g. rocks, nails).
Item that stores charges (e.g. battery, fuel, liquid).

EncumbranceOrRange.description: Encumbrance value — single u32 or a range `[min, max]`.

Energy.description:
Energy measured in Joules.

Used for bionics, vehicle power, and other energy systems.

# Deserialization

Accepts both a bare number (interpreted as Joules) and CDDA-style human-readable strings like `"1 kJ"`, `"500 J"`.

ItemVariant.description:
Item variant entry — the `"variants"` field on items.

Each variant is an alternate appearance/description for the same item.

append.description: Whether variant properties append to base item.

description.description: Alternative description (plain string or object with `str` key).

Length.description:
Length measured in millimeters.

Accepts both a bare number (mm) and CDDA-style strings like `"250 mm"`, `"10 cm"`, `"1 m"`.

LocalizedString.description:
A localized string that may contain translations for multiple languages.

In CDDA JSON, this appears as: ```json { "str": "name", "//~": "context" } { "str_sp": "name" }           // same for singular & plural { "str_pl": "names" }          // explicit plural ``` Or as a plain string `"name"`.

For Stage 1 we store the raw English text. Full i18n support (extracting translations) is deferred.

anyOf.description: A localized object with optional plural and context.

LocalizedText.description:
A localized text value — either a plain string or a structured object with `str`, `str_pl`, `ctxt`, and/or `str_sp` fields.

Examples: - `"A rusty pipe."` - `{"str": "zombie", "str_pl": "zombies"}` - `{"ctxt": "verb", "str": "dented"}`

anyOf.description: Structured text with optional singular, plural, context, and spatial forms.

MaterialList.description:
Material list — can be an array of material references or a single map.

CDDA supports multiple material formats: - `["wood", "steel"]` — array of strings - `[{"type": "paper", "portion": 2}, ...]` — array of objects - `{"paper": 2, "plastic": 1}` — single map of material ID to count

anyOf.description: Single map of material ID to count: `{"paper": 2, "plastic": 1}`.

MaterialPortion.description:
A material with a weight portion (for composite items).

CDDA material objects can have: - `"type"`: material ID (required) - `"portion"`: weight percentage (for composite items) - `"covered_by_mat"`: coverage percentage (for armor layers) - `"thickness"`: material thickness (for armor layers)

MaterialRef.description: Material reference — can be a simple string ("flesh", "steel"), an object with type and portion (for composite materials), or a map of material ID to count (e.g. `{"paper": 2, "plastic": 1}`).

anyOf.description: Composite material with type and portion.
Map of material ID to count (e.g. `{"paper": 2, "plastic": 1}`).

MeleeDamage.description:
CDDA melee damage — the `"melee_damage"` field.

CDDA has evolved through multiple damage formats: 1. Simple bash number: `4` 2. Object with damage-type keys: `{"bash": 4, "cut": 2}` 3. Array of typed entries: `[{"damage_type": "cut", "amount": 2}]`

The array form is the current CDDA standard, but all three are still in use.

Phase.description: Phase of matter for an item.

PocketDef.description: A pocket inside a container item.

ammo_restriction.description: Whether the pocket can be used to store ammo (maps ammo type to capacity).

flag_restriction.description: Item flag restrictions (only items with these flags can go in this pocket).

holster.description: Whether this pocket acts as a holster.

max_contains.description: Number of items that can be stored.

max_item_length.description: Maximum item length to fit in this pocket.

max_volume.description: Maximum volume this pocket can hold.

max_weight.description: Maximum weight this pocket can hold.

min_item_volume.description: Minimum item volume to fit in this pocket.

rigid.description: Whether this pocket is rigid (volume doesn't change when empty).

sealed.description: Whether the pocket is sealed (can't be opened).

oneOf.description: Magazine well (for weapons that accept magazines).
Holster sized for specific weapon types.
Corrosion-resistant outer layer for things like hip pouches.
Pocket that only stores items with certain qualifiers.

RawValue.description: A flexible JSON-like value for catch-all fields where CDDA data can be a string, number, boolean, array, or object. This replaces `serde_json::Value` to avoid pulling in the serde_json dependency for type definitions.

anyOf.description: An object/map of string keys to values.

SnippetCategory.description:
Snippet category reference — the `"snippet_category"` field.

Can be a simple category ID string or a structured snippet list.

anyOf.description: Inline array of snippet objects (CDDA format with `id` and `text` fields).

StringOrArray.description:
A value that can be a single string or an array of strings.

Used by `connect_groups`, `connects_to`, `rotates_to`, and similar fields.

Examples: - `"wall"` → `Single("wall")` - `["wall", "fence"]` → `Multi(vec!["wall", "fence"])`

StructuredText.description: A structured text value from CDDA JSON.

str_sp.description: Spatial form (same for singular and plural).

Time.description:
Game time measured in turns. 1 turn ≈ 1 second.

Accepts both bare numbers (turns) and CDDA-style strings like `"1 h"`, `"30 m"`, `"26 h 12 m"`, `"744m"`.

ToHit.description:
To-hit modifier — the `"to_hit"` field on items.

CDDA can have to_hit as a simple number (legacy) or as an object with grip/length/surface/balance keys.

Examples: - `100` — simple numeric bonus - `{"grip": "weapon", "length": "long", "surface": "any", "balance": "good"}` — structured

ToolQuality.description:
A tool quality entry (e.g. "CUT" quality level 2).

CDDA format is `[["CUT", 2], ["BUTCHER", -18], ...]` — an array of 2-element arrays. This can also be objects `{"id": "CUT", "level": 2}`.

level.description: Level of the quality (can be negative for "anti-qualities").

ToolRequirement.description:
Tool requirement — a single tool ID string, or a map of tool IDs to counts.

CDDA uses `"tool": "syringe"` for single-tool requirements and `"tool": { "syringe": 1 }` for tool-with-count requirements.

anyOf.description: Map of tool IDs to counts: `{ "syringe": 1 }`.

TypedDamage.description: A damage entry with explicit type and amount (current CDDA format).

UseAction.description:
Item use action — the `"use_action"` field.

Can be a simple string ID referencing a built-in action, or an object with `"type"` and optional extra parameters.

anyOf.description: Tool action with tool ID and charges: `["CROWBAR", 0]`.
Array of actions (CDDA format where use_action is an array).
Catch-all for any action type not specifically modeled.

UseActionDef.description: A use action definition object with the most common fields. CDDA has many action types; this covers the majority.

moves_slow.description: Slow move speed (alternative to moves for firestarters etc).

need_wielding.description: Whether the item needs to be wielded.

UseActionEffect.description: An effect reference in a use action — either a simple effect ID or an object.

anyOf.description: Object with effect type and parameters.

UseActionItem.description: An item reference in a use action.

UseActionTool.description: A tool reference in a use action.

VitaminContents.description:
Vitamin cost mapping — the `"vitamins"` field on comestibles.

Example: `[["calcium", 2], ["iron", 6], ["meat_allergen", 1]]`

VitaminEntry.description:
A single vitamin entry: `["vitamin_id", amount]`.

Amount can be a number or a string like "14 mg" or "500 μg".

Volume.description:
Volume measured in milliliters.

CDDA internally stores volumes in mL (1 mL = 0.001 L).

Accepts both a bare number (mL) and CDDA-style strings like `"250 ml"`, `"1 L"`.

Weight.description:
Weight measured in grams.

Accepts both a bare number (grams) and CDDA-style strings like `"100 g"`, `"1 kg"`.
